topicName: Data Lineage, Catalogs, and Metadata Management
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Data Lineage, Catalogs, and Metadata Management in Data Warehousing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"As modern data architectures scale, understanding the origin, movement, transformation, and ultimate consumption of data becomes critical. Metadata management, data catalogs, and data lineage form the foundational triad that ensures data trustworthiness, compliance, and discoverability in enterprise data warehouses."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Metadata Types"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Metadata is broadly categorized into three distinct types within a data warehouse ecosystem:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Technical Metadata: Schema definitions, data types, table sizes, storage locations, index details, and ETL job schedules."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Operational Metadata: Job execution logs, run times, success/failure status, error messages, and resource consumption metrics."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Business Metadata: Data governance tags, glossaries, ownership, data stewardship, sensitivity classifications, and compliance markers."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Data Catalogs"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"A data catalog acts as a centralized repository for all enterprise metadata. It enables data consumers to search, discover, and understand data assets. Below is an example of querying a system information schema in a cloud data warehouse to extract technical metadata for a custom catalog synchronization script."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"SELECT table_catalog, table_schema, table_name, column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'analytics_prod' ORDER BY table_name, ordinal_position;"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Tracking Data Lineage"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Data lineage provides a visual and programmatic map of data flow from its source systems, through staging and transformation layers, to final reporting dashboards. Lineage can be implemented via parsing SQL queries or orchestrator logs."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"INSERT INTO warehouse.dim_customer_history (customer_id, effective_date, status) SELECT src.id, CURRENT_DATE(), src.status FROM staging.raw_customers AS src WHERE src.updated_at >= CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL '1' DAY;"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"By analyzing the SQL statement above, a lineage parser automatically extracts the relationship: staging.raw_customers provides the source data, transforming it via a conditional filter, and populates the warehouse.dim_customer_history target table."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Metadata Management"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Automate metadata harvesting using native warehouse hooks and orchestration tools to avoid manual documentation drift."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enforce data governance policies by requiring business glossary definitions before promoting tables to production schemas."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Integrate data lineage with impact analysis tools to preview downstream dashboard failures before modifying upstream schemas."}]
